node.title: PMA three-petal projective Johnson bound
node.statement: Distinct primitive coefficient pairs in one three-petal mu-basis module have split core-root sets intersecting in at most e-1. A Johnson second-moment argument therefore bounds their number by N(d-e+1)/(d^2-N(e-1)) whenever the denominator is positive. This pays every rate-quarter M=4,t=3 cell with a uniform 16n^3 per-source bound and every positive-denominator rate-half cell, including all backgrounds b<=6. The only surviving three-petal cells form an explicit nonpositive-denominator rate-half top-defect tail.
